fields.v: AI-Assisted R&D TMG, Huawei; SMAT Lab, Beihang University; CodeWisdom Lab, Fudan University (contributors: Li, L., Hu, H., Zhang, T., Peng, X., Mao, F., et al.; 30 contributors listed) (2026). OpenHarmony Bench: Evaluating LLMs and Coding Agents on OpenHarmony App Development. arXiv:2608.16022v1 [cs.SE], 17 Aug 2026. https://bench.matrix.openharmony.cn/
Preprint — arXiv:2608.16022v1 (cs.SE), technical report; no venue stated
Industry and academia: AI-Assisted R&D TMG, Huawei (China); SMAT Lab, Beihang University; CodeWisdom Lab, Fudan University (per-author affiliations Not stated)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — app-level benchmark OpenHarmony Bench v1.0 (153 tasks: new-feature, spec-driven, bug-fix; build-and-test pipeline with executable UI checks) and comparison of 8 LLMs under the fixed DevEco Code agent, 3 runs each

No SDD approach named. The benchmark has a 'spec-driven' task source (standardized scenario-level specifications with explicit acceptance structure, normalized into specification -> scenario -> F-point) next to requirement-style new-feature requests and bug reports. Agent: DevEco Code (OpenHarmony-SIG) version 0.1.0-1.3. Models: GLM-5.1, GLM-5.2, Qwen3.7-Max, Qwen3.8-Max-Preview, Kimi-K2.7-Code, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek-V4-Pro (display names)

Per task: task description (new-feature request, median 119 chars; spec-driven scenario-level specification, median 589 chars, e.g. four scenarios for a chat input; bug report, median 107 chars) + runnable ArkTS base project at a base commit. Hidden from agent: reference solution and Hypium executable checks (F-points). Prompt template: (1) task definition; (2) spec content and environment; (3) code generation instructions

Evaluation pipeline: workspace initialization -> agent execution (task description, project context, system instruction, prompt template, tools) -> diff recording -> first build -> bounded compile repair (max 5 iterations, build output only) -> behaviour validation (install, launch, Python Hypium UI checks). No SDD phases (spec, plan, tasks) prescribed to the agent
None during runs. Curators review specifications, reference implementations and tests during construction (at least two curators validate each test)
Specification format only (spec-driven source: scenario-level specifications given as agent input), run by an agent; no named SDD workflow
Not classifiable. Authors' wording: 'standardized specification-driven incremental development', 'specification-following'
fields.why: No named SDD approach; the spec-driven source gives the agent a scenario-level specification written before the code, which another reader could classify as spec-first.
fields.doubt: Não há abordagem SDD nomeada, mas as tarefas spec-driven partem de especificações por cenário escritas antes do código; decide se é spec-first ou 'não classificável'.

Criterion: task complete = final build succeeds and all executable checks pass. 3 independent full-suite runs each; DevEco Code 0.1.0-1.3, temperature 0, context 200K, reasoning budget 65.5K. For every configuration: quality: no criterion stated by the authors (task-level completion rule only, no configuration-level threshold); cost: no criterion stated by the authors

Project/tasks: 153 OpenHarmony Bench v1.0 tasks (snapshot 2026.7.31) in three sources. Configurations: 8 models under one agent (DevEco Code); the task sources (requirement-style vs spec-driven vs bug report) are compared descriptively but on different tasks. Baseline: no-op (0%) floor, reference solutions 100% ceiling. Held constant: agent framework and version, task split, system instruction, prompt template, tool access, environment, build and scoring scripts, temperature, context window, reasoning budget. Acceptance tests: hidden Hypium executable checks (fail-to-pass). Repetitions: 3 full-suite runs per configuration, mean and min-max. Human intervention: none; up to 5 automatic compile-repair iterations with build output only; no token or time cap

GLM-5.2 highest overall TC (58.39%), then Kimi-K3 (57.30%) and Qwen3.8-Max-Preview (55.99%) as a leading group; MiniMax-M3 lowest (48.36%). Newer generations beat predecessors within the evaluated families. Final build 94.77-100% vs TC 48.36-58.39%: many projects build without the required behaviour. By source: bug-fix highest (60.56-75.12%), new-feature middle (53.13-63.54%), spec-driven lowest (24.00-34.67%, no configuration above 35%) under all-F-points scoring. Qwen3.8-Max-Preview lowest tokens and time. Ranks are descriptive; ranges overlap; no significance tests

Separated build success from behavioural correctness and showed a leading group, but adjacent ranks not statistically separated (Kimi-K3 range contains GLM-5.2 mean; Kimi-K2.7-Code and DeepSeek-V4-Pro tie at 52.07). Repeatability: 3 runs with observed ranges (e.g. Qwen3.8 new-feature identical in all runs); artefacts, scripts and snapshot identifiers released. Limitations stated: single agent framework, so results are DevEco Code-model configurations; 3 runs give no inferential interval; bug-fix tasks from public PRs may be in pre-training data; token counts not comparable across providers; wall-clock time environment-dependent

Limitations: fixed DevEco Code framework (no comparison of independent agent frameworks); three runs only, no confidence intervals or statistical separation; possible pre-training exposure of bug-fix source; public release may cause contamination over time (recommend updated snapshots and trajectory audits for reward hacking). Gap: buildability is near-saturated while behavioural correctness, especially spec-following, is not

Individual author list not given on the title page (only groups; contributors list p. 17). Possible inconsistency: Figure 5 spec-driven bars (as extracted from the PDF text) read 28.0 for DeepSeek and 24.0 for MiniMax, while Table 6 gives DeepSeek-V4-Pro 24.00 and MiniMax-M3 28.00; values here from Table 6 (check the figure). Source-level comparison confounded: spec-driven tasks have more F-points (2.78 vs 1.00) and larger reference patches (12 files / 489.5 LOC), and are different tasks, so lower TC is not an effect of specifications alone. Data and replication package: tasks, reference solutions, tests, evaluation and aggregation scripts, leaderboard at https://bench.matrix.openharmony.cn/. No pre-registration. Programming language: ArkTS (evaluation scripts Python)
